summary.headline: SBI Funds Management Q2 FY27: QAAUM up 10% YoY to INR 13.14 lakh crore; Q2 cost step-up flagged as partly one-time; H1 PAT INR 1,566 crore.
summary.overview: Mutual fund QAAUM reached INR 13.14 lakh crore (up 10% YoY) with a 15% industry share, and active QAAUM grew 9% YoY to INR 8.99 lakh crore. H1 FY27 operating revenue rose 12% YoY to INR 2,336 crore and operating profit rose 11% to INR 1,797 crore. Management said Q2 costs rose sharply sequentially on one-time technology and senior hiring spends, while equity yield was guided at about 62-63 bps. The call also covered alternatives (AIF QAAUM up 27% YoY to INR 7,437 crore), SIP momentum, and investor sentiment during volatile markets.

financial_highlights.change: Declined on one-time relocation of a large mandate; revenue impact called immaterial
+12% from INR 2,089 crore in H1 FY26
+11% from INR 1,626 crore in H1 FY26

segments.name: Active equity
segments.commentary: Active equity QAAUM INR 8,986 billion, up 9% YoY; equity yield about 62-63 bps in Q2 FY27 per management.

segments.name: Debt
segments.commentary: Debt yield in the range of about 34-35 bps; management said debt AUM industry-wide moderated 5% YoY.

segments.name: Liquid
segments.commentary: Liquid yield about 11-12 bps; liquid QAAUM INR 1.2 lakh crore, up 31% YoY.

segments.name: Passive
segments.commentary: Largest passive asset manager with QAAUM INR 4.15 lakh crore, up 11% YoY.

segments.name: Alternatives (PMS, advisory, AIF, offshore)
segments.commentary: Non-MF book roughly equal to MF book; ex-advisory yield about 35-40 bps on offshore advisory and alternatives. Offshore funds about INR 42,100 crore AUM.

guidance_outlook: Q2 employee and other costs carry one-time tech and senior hiring spend; management said Q2 cost should be treated as the new run-rate base, with some moderation.
Management said about 50-60% of the incremental Q2 spend will recur (senior hires and continuing AI/cloud investment); the one-time portion is expected to fall 30-40%.
Some tech costs will persist (cloud compute, AI); own data centre going live in a couple of months, which may moderate cloud costs.
ESOP policy already in place; no exceptional ESOP cost expected in coming quarters.
Category III AIF launch planned in coming months; Category II capability being built under new alternatives head.
Four of six SEBI-approved SIF options still to be launched.
Management expects revenue to stay neutral under the new SEBI pricing methodology effective 1 April.
capex_capacity: Own data centre going live in a couple of months, expected to shift cloud workloads to on-premise.
Investments in AI, cloud infrastructure and key senior hires described as ongoing capability spend.
Launched five new products in Q2, including one SIF; Magnum Equity Ex-Top 100 Long Short Fund NFO closed as one of the largest in its category.
GIFT City franchise scaling with SBI Global Thematic Advantage Fund launched.
Aarambh assisted digital onboarding platform showcased; 94% of transactions digital, InvesTap has over 4.3 million registered users.
demand_pricing: Industry: QAAUM INR 87.5 trillion, up 13% YoY; monthly SIP inflows record INR 32,490 crore in September 2026; September net sales about INR 38,000 crore.
SBI MF: quarterly average AUM market share 15%; SIP monthly inflows about INR 3,900 crore; SBI channel contributes about 20% of net inflows, similar to its AUM share.
SIF market share about 16%-plus per management; SIF AUM rose from about INR 35 billion to INR 44 billion in the quarter, driven by a new launch.
B30 locations account for about two-thirds of SIP inflows; 98% of customers have been invested for more than 36 months per management.
Equity yield was described as stable to slightly lower QoQ, with yields up about 1 bp YoY per management; no category-level change from distributor commissions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and other expenses rise sharply QoQ and YoY, and what is the full-year outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited one-time tech (cloud and AI) and senior hiring spend in Q2, not expected to repeat in Q3. Analyst Shreyas Pimple was told the Q2 cost base is the run-rate; the QoQ increase was about INR 27-28 crore, and Q1 had write-backs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the slight yield dip QoQ due to telescopic structure or something else; any distribution-mix change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no category-level yield change and no change in distribution cost; the dip reflects asset mix, with equity yield 62-63 bps, debt 34-35 bps and liquid 11-12 bps.

qa_highlights.question: How is investor sentiment tracking, and any divergence between assisted and fintech channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SIP and hybrid categories are seeing rising demand; new investors are more anxious, while long-tenure investors are steady. The company has not studied the assisted versus fintech split, but observed that fintech platforms are also educating investors.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AIF strategy and capital commitment?
qa_highlights.answer: Company is building private equity and private credit teams under a new alternatives head; no capital allocation figure given, with the business starting as an internal division.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PMS AUM decline, and what is the MF vs non-MF split?
qa_highlights.answer: A large investor mandate was reallocated, reducing PMS and advisory AUM with revenue impact described as immaterial. MF AUM is about INR 13.5 lakh crore, with a roughly 50:50 split against non-MF.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any SBI-channel versus other-channel flow split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the SBI channel is about 20% of net inflows, unchanged QoQ; bank and other distributor channels are where share gains are now coming from.

risks_watch: Sustainability of cost run-rate: management said about 50-60% of the Q2 increase recurs and tech costs will not fully fall away.
Yield compression: QoQ yield dip flagged by analysts while peers saw increases.
Non-MF AUM volatility from large mandate reallocations (PMS and advisory).
Fund performance dispersion: about 70% of funds in top two quartiles over 5 years, but about 45% over 3 years.
New-investor anxiety in volatile markets; Nifty YTD correction of 8.2% cited.
Upcoming SEBI MF-only PMS proposal, effective April next year per management; team to be built.
summary.management_tone: Confident on flows, SIP growth and market share, but guarded and somewhat evasive on cost quantification, with answers on the recurring cost split varying across speakers. Management was open about the one-time nature of Q2 spend.
key_quotes: Yes, we have heavily invested in technology and human resources in the last quarter, and there were some one‑off expenses related to strengthening our cloud infrastructure and enhancing our AI‑driven systems.
So SBI channel contributes to around 20% of the net inflows, which is also like the same level as AUM, similar in the last quarter as well.
The cost structure which was one-time will go down by 30 -40%. So , 60% will be kind of recurring.

adds.what: Own data centre going live (on-premise cloud shift)

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management says revenue stays neutral under new SEBI pricing from 1 April, and H1 FY27 operating revenue grew 12% YoY with Q2 costs flagged as new run-rate, with growth backed only by launches (5 new products, SIF) and an AIF launch plan rather than concrete capacity.

mgmt.note: Management referenced a new alternatives head building Category II capability; no date of change given in brief.
initiatives: Category III AIF launch in coming months
